ABEBA TRADING PLC (fictional company, Addis Ababa)
EMPLOYEE HR POLICY HANDBOOK
Effective date: January 1, 2026

This handbook is a demo document for a learning project. It is loosely inspired by Ethiopian labor practice but is not legal advice.


SECTION 1: WORKING HOURS

1.1 The normal working week is Monday to Friday, with working hours from 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM. This includes a one-hour lunch break from 12:30 PM to 1:30 PM.

1.2 Employees work a maximum of 8 hours per day and 48 hours per week.

1.3 Overtime must be approved in writing by the employee's line manager before the work is done. Overtime on a normal working day is paid at 1.25 times the hourly rate. Overtime on a weekly rest day (Saturday and Sunday) is paid at 2 times the hourly rate. Overtime on a public holiday is paid at 2.5 times the hourly rate.

1.4 Employees who arrive more than 15 minutes late three times in one month will receive a written reminder from their manager.


SECTION 2: ANNUAL LEAVE

SECTION 2: ANNUAL LEAVE

2.1 Every employee who has completed one year of service is entitled to 16 working days of paid annual leave.

2.2 After the first year, one additional day of annual leave is added for every two years of service. For example, an employee with five years of service receives 18 days.

2.3 Annual leave requests must be submitted to the line manager at least 14 days before the planned start date. The manager will reply within 5 working days.

2.4 Employees may carry over a maximum of 5 unused annual leave days into the next calendar year. Carried-over days must be used by March 31, or they are lost.

2.5 Annual leave is not paid out in cash, except when an employee leaves the company, in which case unused days are paid out at the final salary rate.


SECTION 3: SICK LEAVE

3.1 An employee who is sick must inform their line manager by phone or message before 9:00 AM on the first day of absence.

3.2 For absences of 3 days or more, the employee must provide a medical certificate from a recognized health facility.

3.3 With a valid medical certificate, an employee receives full pay for the first month of sick leave. For the following two months, the employee receives 50 percent of their salary. After that, sick leave is unpaid.

3.4 Sick leave does not reduce annual leave days.


SECTION 4: MATERNITY AND PATERNITY LEAVE

SECTION 4: MATERNITY AND PATERNITY LEAVE

4.1 A pregnant employee is entitled to paid maternity leave of 120 days in total. This is made up of up to 30 days before the expected date of birth and 90 days after birth.

4.2 Maternity leave is paid at full salary. The employee must submit a medical certificate confirming the expected date of birth at least 30 days before starting leave.

4.3 A male employee whose spouse gives birth is entitled to 5 consecutive working days of paid paternity leave, starting from the date of birth.

4.4 Employees returning from maternity leave will be given their previous position or an equivalent one at the same salary.


SECTION 5: OTHER LEAVE

5.1 Marriage leave: an employee who gets married receives 3 paid days off.

5.2 Bereavement leave: an employee receives 3 paid days off on the death of a spouse, child, parent, brother, or sister.

5.3 Public holidays are paid days off for all employees. The official list of Ethiopian public holidays is posted on the staff notice board at the beginning of each year.


SECTION 6: PROBATION

6.1 All new employees serve a probation period of 45 days.

6.2 During probation, the line manager will meet with the employee at least once every two weeks to give feedback.

6.3 During probation, either the employee or the company may end the contract without notice.

6.4 Annual leave does not accrue during probation.

6.5 At the end of probation, the manager will confirm the employee's permanent position in writing.


SECTION 7: RESIGNATION AND NOTICE

7.1 An employee who wishes to resign must give 30 days written notice to the line manager and the HR department.

7.2 The company may ask the employee to work through the notice period or may agree to a shorter period in writing.

7.3 Before the last working day, the employee must return all company property, including laptop, ID card, and keys.

7.4 The final salary and any unused annual leave payment will be paid within 7 working days after the last working day.

7.5 On request, HR will issue a service certificate showing the employee's job title and dates of employment.


SECTION 8: PAYROLL

SECTION 8: PAYROLL

8.1 Salaries are paid on the 25th of each month directly into the employee's bank account. If the 25th falls on a weekend or holiday, salary is paid on the last working day before it.

8.2 Income tax and the employee's pension contribution are deducted from salary by the company and sent to the relevant authorities.

8.3 Payslips are sent to each employee's company email address on the day of payment.


SECTION 9: CODE OF CONDUCT

SECTION 9: CODE OF CONDUCT

9.1 Employees must treat colleagues, customers, and suppliers with respect. Harassment and discrimination of any kind are not tolerated.

9.2 Employees must not accept gifts worth more than 1,000 birr from suppliers or customers without telling HR.

9.3 Company information is confidential and must not be shared with outsiders without written approval from a manager.

9.4 Serious breaches of this code can lead to a written warning, suspension, or dismissal, after the employee has had a chance to respond.


SECTION 10: HR CONTACTS

10.1 Questions about this handbook can be sent to hr@abebatrading.example or asked in person at the HR office on the second floor, Room 204.

10.2 The HR office is open Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM.
